key_insight: UNIEGO learns a richer egocentric video representation by using multiple stronger teachers as proxies, so a model trained on wearable-camera video can inherit knowledge from other viewpoints, modalities, and foundation models. This helps bridge the gap between what egocentric video alone shows and what full human action understanding requires.
problem_solved: Egocentric video is inherently incomplete: it comes from a single wearable viewpoint and often misses information that is visible from other perspectives or modalities. The paper addresses how to build a more expressive representation from egocentric video alone without requiring extra inputs at deployment.
method: Uses a hierarchical multi-teacher distillation framework.
Treats proxies from complementary sources (e.g., other viewpoints, modalities, and foundation models) as mediators of richer knowledge.
Trains a deployable egocentric model that learns from these teachers during training but operates on egocentric video only at inference.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to boost egocentric video understanding without changing deployment constraints. It is useful for applications like action recognition, robotics, AR/VR, and wearable AI where only first-person video is available.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing egocentric video feeding into a student model via multiple teacher/proxy branches.
An icon-based comparison of viewpoints, modalities, and foundation models as complementary knowledge sources.
A hierarchical distillation flowchart illustrating teacher-to-proxy-to-student knowledge transfer.
A before/after performance chart showing gains from unified representation learning.
paper_title: UNIEGO: Proxies as Mediators for Unified Egocentric Video Representation Learning
paper_authors: Wenhao Chi, Arkaprava Sinha, Dominick Reilly, Hieu Le, Srijan Das
